findings.message: Exploitation statement incomplete: all 12 CVE records carry a CISA ADP SSVC entry (updated 2026-11-05) with Exploitation: none

content_preview.title: PostgreSQL Anonymizer 3.3 fixes 12 CVEs that Dalibo calls critical; CVE records score them 3.5 to 6.5
content_preview.summary: Dalibo's PostgreSQL Anonymizer 3.3 fixes 12 CVEs. Its announcement calls them critical; the CVE records give CVSS 3.1 base scores of 3.5 to 6.5, and none of the records mentions superuser access, which the announcement cites.
content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Overview

Dalibo's PostgreSQL Anonymizer 3.3 fixes 12 vulnerabilities. [Dalibo's announcement on postgresql.org](https://www.postgresql.org/about/news/postgresql-anonymizer-33-major-security-update-3423/) says: "Version 3.3 includes fixes for 12 critical vulnerabilities allowing some users to gain superuser privileges under certain circumstances or allowing masked users to access personal information." The CVE records for the 12 identifiers, which the Herald read in the CVE Program's record s...

editor_notes.content_quality: Compact, well-structured Briefing (693 words, range 300-800). Quotes the announcement and tabulates the 12 CVE records by CVSS score without editorialising. The 'What We Don't Know' section is honest about what the sources do not establish. Title is 101 characters (under the 150 limit); nothing to flag.
editor_notes.source_verification: Snapshots read from disk (gunzip -c), all 14 fetched with HTTP 200, no archive fallback, no bot-check pages, no suspicious_patterns entries; every snapshot's sha256 recomputed and equal to the manifest value. Host allowlist: cveawg.mitre.org (line 3021, vetted Oct 2026) and postgresql.org (line 1167) are both listed; no allowlist addition needed. source-0 (Dalibo announcement, postgresql.org/about/news/...-3423): confirms 'Posted on 2026-10-28 by Dalibo', dateline 'Eymoutiers, France, October 27th, 2026', and the exact sentence 'Version 3.3 includes fixes for 12 critical vulnerabilities allowing some users to gain superuser privileges under certain circumstances or allowing masked users to access personal information.' (line-wrapped in the HTML, verbatim otherwise); the extension description quote; 'All users should upgrade the extension to version 3.3 as soon as possible.'; 'Subqueries in masking rules are now forbidden'; 'Inlining of functions is disabled for transparent dynamic masking'; masked roles forbidden from executing functions with SQL-standard bodies (paraphrased, not quoted); 'It is also strongly advised to change the value of the anon.salt GUC parameter.'; the credit to Alexander Kukushkin and Ilya Staroverov for reporting. The announcement lists 12 distinct CVE ids; they are the same 12 as the 12 CVE URLs cited (recounted: 12 entries, 12 distinct ids, no duplicates). The announcement itself gives no CVSS score, no rating scale and does not use the word 'superuser' per CVE, only in the general sentence. source-1 (E-Maj 5.0.1 post, ...-3425): confirms 'Posted on 2026-10-31 by Philippe Beaudoin', the quoted sentence 'This version mainly fixes a vulnerability encountered in all previous versions, allowing some users to gain superuser privileges under certain circumstances.', 'Users are strongly encouraged to update their installed version as soon as possible.', compatibility with Postgres 14 to 19, and no CVE identifier anywhere in the page (grep for 'CVE' returns nothing). The post's title also says 'Major Security Update', but unlike the Dalibo post it does not use the word 'critical'; the article says 'similar language', which holds. sources 2-13 (CVE Program records, raw JSON from cveawg.mitre.org, parsed with jq): all 12 have state PUBLISHED, assignerShortName 'PostgreSQL' (the PostgreSQL project's CNA), datePublished 2026-10-28 (17:31 to 17:31 UTC), affected vendor 'DALIBO', product 'PostgreSQL Anonymizer', versions lessThan 3.3.0, descriptions saying fixed/resolved in 3.3.0 and later. CNA CVSS 3.1 base scores recomputed per record: 6.5 CVE-2026-105620 and CVE-2026-110181; 5.7 CVE-2026-105616, -105617, -105618; 4.8 CVE-2026-105619; 4.7 CVE-2026-105613 and -105614; 4.3 CVE-2026-110182 and -110183; 3.5 CVE-2026-105612 and -105615. That is 2+3+1+2+2+2 = 12, minimum 3.5, maximum 6.5, severities Low (two) and Medium (ten): the title range '3.5 to 6.5' and every row of the article's list are correct, and each CVE is attributed to the right score. Per-CVE descriptions match the article's glosses (the DoS label for the two memory-allocation issues is the announcement's own wording; the records describe memory exhaustion leading to OOM-kill and cluster-wide crash recovery). Herald's own check: grep -i 'superuser|super-user|super user' over all 12 raw records (CNA and ADP containers, descriptions, workarounds) returns no match, so 'none of the 12 records mentions superuser access' is correct and is labelled as the Herald's own in the body. Workarounds: exactly three records say 'None' (CVE-2026-105612, -105618, -105620); the other nine give steps; CVE-2026-105617 says 'Disconnect active sessions after changing a masking rule' (verbatim). Credits: 10 of 12 credit Ilya Staroverov, CVE-2026-105613 and -105614 credit Alexander Kukushkin (Herald count of 10 is right and labelled). Quantifiers 'all 12 records were published on 2026-10-28' and 'all name DALIBO as the vendor' hold item by item. Content not in the article but found: each record also carries a CISA ADP Vulnrichment container (dateUpdated 2026-11-05, i.e. after the 2026-11-04 submission) with SSVC options Exploitation: none, Automatable: no, Technical Impact: partial; this makes the article's 'Neither the announcement nor the records say' about exploitation incomplete (clarification filed). Each record also links a Dalibo GitLab issue (not cited by the article). Independence recount: 0 independent sources. The two postgresql.org pages are the project's news channel carrying Dalibo's own announcement and E-Maj's own announcement; the 12 CVE records were published by the PostgreSQL project's CNA but are derived from Dalibo's/the reporters' disclosure and name Dalibo as vendor, so they are a second first-party record, not an independent investigation. The article says so plainly. Briefing category: no independence requirement. Anthropic disclosure: not required - the subject is Dalibo's PostgreSQL Anonymizer and the PostgreSQL CVE records; Anthropic is not mentioned in the headline, summary, lead or any credit line.
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: All dates, versions, CVE ids, scores, counts, quotes and names verified against raw source text (see source_verification). No fabricated or misattributed specific found. The summary's three claims (announcement calls them critical; CVSS 3.1 scores 3.5 to 6.5; none of the records mentions superuser access) are each supported; the third is a Herald check, labelled as such in the body. Absence and quantifier sentences tested against every snapshot: 'none of the 12 records describes superuser access' holds; 'the post names no CVE identifier' (E-Maj) holds; 'No independent news coverage ... was found' is scoped to the Herald's search and no cited source contradicts it; the exploitation sentence is the one that is now incomplete (CISA ADP SSVC 'Exploitation: none' added 2026-11-05). No relative dates. The 'critical' versus CVSS contrast is stated as two facts; the article does not claim either is wrong, but it does not say that 'critical' is the vendor's own descriptive word (not a CVSS band) and that the scores are the CNA's, so a clarification is filed.
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral. No blame on Dalibo, no suggestion of exaggeration; the article says 'Neither source explains the difference'. The headline juxtaposition is a fair factual contrast of two quotable figures; the clarification adds the missing note that vendor wording and CVSS scores are different measures.
editor_notes.originality: No earlier Herald article covers PostgreSQL Anonymizer, Dalibo or E-Maj (grep over src/content/articles and submissions finds only unrelated substring matches). New topic.
concerns: Exploitation sentence incomplete: every record now carries a CISA ADP SSVC entry (updated 2026-11-05) with 'Exploitation: none'. The article was submitted 2026-11-04 so it could not have read it; filed as a clarification.
Headline/summary juxtaposition of the vendor's word 'critical' with CVSS scores omits that the two are different measures and that the scores are the PostgreSQL CNA's; filed as a clarification.

Minor, no correction: the gloss for CVE-2026-105620 says 'a masked role reading authentic data', while the record only says the sub-query data is not masked (the announcement's phrasing 'masked users' and the vector's PR:L/C:H are consistent with it); the 'denial-of-service' label for the two memory-allocation CVEs is the announcement's wording rather than the records'.
First-party-only sourcing: no independent outlet; documented honestly in the article.
recommendations: For vendor-versus-CVSS contrasts, say in one clause that a vendor's descriptive word and a CVSS band are different measures and name who assigned the scores.
Before submitting a CVE-based article, re-check the records for ADP (CISA) containers, which are added after the CNA publishes and can answer exploitation questions.
editor_notes.overall_assessment: Accurate, neutral and honestly scoped Briefing whose numbers, quotes and dates all check out against raw source text; two subordinate clarifications (CISA exploitation assessment added after submission; vendor wording versus CNA-assigned CVSS scores) are filed in a corrections record and neither touches the headline's factual content. Verdict: APPROVE_WITH_CORRECTIONS. Featured candidacy: 1 - accurate security-fix coverage of a niche PostgreSQL extension for a defined developer/DBA audience
